chapter.v:
A good
reputation is a much better choice than plenty of money; respect is better than silver and gold.

The rich
and the poor have this in common: the Lord created them all.

If you're
sensible you see danger coming and get out of the way; but stupid people just keep going and pay for it.

The reward
you receive for being humble and respecting the Lord is wealth, honor, and life.

Thorns and
traps lie in the path of crooked people; those who value their lives will stay away from them.

Teach children
the right way to live, and when they grow up they'll go on doing so.

The rich
rule the poor, and borrowers are slaves to their lenders.

Those who
sow injustice will reap disaster, and the angry beatings they inflict on others will be stopped.

If you're
generous, you'll be blessed, for you share your food with those in need.

Get rid
of the scornful, and you'll get rid of conflict too—no more arguments or insults!

Anyone who
loves sincerity and a gracious way of speaking will have the king as their friend.

The Lord
watches over true knowledge, but counteracts the words of liars.

Lazy people
make claims like, “There's a lion outside! I might be killed if I go out there!”

The seductive
words of an immoral woman are a dangerous trap—if the Lord's angry with you, then you'll fall right in.

Children are
naturally foolish; physical correction helps them to see sense.

If you
oppress the poor to make yourself rich, or if you're generous to the rich, you'll end up poor yourself.

Pay attention
and listen to the words of the wise, and think carefully about my teachings—

for it's
good to keep them in mind so you can be ready to share them.

I'm explaining
this to you today so you can trust in the Lord—yes, you!

Haven't I
written down for you thirty sayings of advice and wisdom?

They are
to make it clear to you what's right and true, so you can give a truthful explanation to those who sent you.

For you
shouldn't steal from the poor just because they're poor; and you shouldn't crush those with limited means in court,

for the
Lord will plead their case, and he will take back whatever was stolen from them.

Don't make
friends with someone who gets upset easily; don't associate with angry people,

in case
you learn to be like them and make a mess of your life.

Don't shake
hands and guarantee someone's debt,

for if
you can't pay, why should your bed be taken away from beneath you?

Don't move
ancient boundary markers that your forefathers put in place.

If you
see someone skilled in what they do, they'll work for kings and not for ordinary people.
